newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine greets U.S.-Russia talks, rues differences.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine greets U.S.-Russia talks, rues differences.

text.p: Ukraine on Saturday welcomed the outcome of the U.S.-Russian summit in Helsinki but said it regretted the failure to overcome differences over plans by the NATO military alliance to admit new members.
"Ukraine welcomes the dialogue between Russia and the United States on issues of exceptional interest to all nations of the North Atlantic region," a foreign ministry statement said.
"It is regrettable that the differences in opinions between the United States and Russia on the problem of NATO expansion could not be removed," it added.

The statement was issued in response to talks in Finland between Russian President Boris Yeltsin and U.S. President Bill Clinton at which they agreed to sign a charter building a new relationship between Moscow and the Western alliance.
Ukraine is not seeking immediate entry to NATO but does not share Russia's hostility to its enlargement eastwards.

The statement also welcomed the presidents' "adherence to the principle of respecting the sovereignty and territorial integrity of all countries and also their inseparable right to choose their own method of security".
It welcomed efforts to create the charter deal, similar to one being negotiated with Kiev which diplomats say could also be signed at a summit of the alliance in July in Madrid.
But such a deal between NATO and Russia "must assist in strengthening European security and not destroy the fundamental security interests of other interested states," it added.

Ukrainian-Russian relations have been marred ever since Kiev won independence in 1991 by their failure to agree exactly how to settle the issue of the Black Sea Fleet, based on Ukraine's Crimean peninsula which is claimed by Russian nationalists.
Yeltsin has cancelled a string of trips to Kiev to sign a friendship treaty because of the disagreement.
